turns.doctor_question: Hello, thank you for coming in today. What brings you to see me?
turns.patient_response: Well, what brings me in is... I just keep going back over my jobs again and again. I'm an electrician, and I find myself constantly checking breakers, labels, torque marks, taking photos of the panels... sometimes I even drive all the way back to a job site after I've left just to be sure. It's getting to the point where a simple install takes me way longer than it should, and people at work are starting to notice.

symptom_reasoning.S066: The patient describes excessive, repetitive checking behaviors (checking breakers, labels, photos, and driving back to job sites to verify work) that interfere with work efficiency.

turns.doctor_question: Do you feel anxious or upset if you're not able to go back and check your work?
turns.patient_response:
Yeah, very much so. If I try to just drive away and not go back to double-check those breakers or look at the photos I took... I just can't let it go. My stomach kind of ties up in knots. 

Like I was just saying, that's exactly why these simple installs are taking me so long now. I just can't move on to the next thing unless I go back and do all that checking again. If I don't, I'm just a wreck thinking I missed a torque mark or messed up a label somewhere, and it just eats at me until I finally give in and go back to the site.

symptom_reasoning.S066: The patient describes repetitive checking behaviors (checking breakers, reviewing photos, and repeatedly returning to work sites) that they feel compelled to perform to relieve distress and anxiety about potential mistakes.

turns.doctor_question: Do you find yourself having unwanted thoughts or mental images about something bad happening if you don't check your work, like a fire or an accident?
turns.patient_response: Yeah, exactly. Even after I know I checked a panel or a disconnect, this thought just keeps barging in on me. I start thinking that maybe I missed one loose neutral, or left something undone that could start a fire. I try to shake it off, tell myself I did it right, but it just... it follows me all the way home. I can't stop picturing a house burning down because of something I missed.

symptom_reasoning.S065: The patient confirms experiencing recurrent, intrusive, and distressing thoughts and mental images of causing a fire, which persist despite attempts to dismiss them.

turns.doctor_question: When you have these thoughts about something bad happening, do you feel driven to do certain things, like checking or taking pictures, to try to reduce your anxiety or prevent the bad thing from happening?
turns.patient_response:
Yeah, that's exactly it. Like I was saying earlier, that's the whole reason I keep going back over my jobs. I get that image in my head, and I just feel like I have to do those things to make the feeling stop. 

I have to check the breakers again, look at the labels and the torque marks, or scroll through the photos I took on my phone. Sometimes driving all the way back to the site is the only thing that makes the panic go away. It does bring the anxiety down for a bit, but... well, it's getting to the point where a basic install takes me way longer than it should. And like I mentioned, the guys at work are definitely starting to notice that I'm dragging behind.

symptom_reasoning.S066: The patient explicitly confirms feeling driven to perform repetitive checking rituals, review photos, and re-visit job sites to relieve panic and anxiety triggered by intrusive thoughts.

turns.doctor_question: How much time do these checking behaviors and thoughts take up in your day, and have they caused you any significant problems at work or in your personal life?
turns.patient_response:
Well, it takes up a lot of time. Honestly, it's hard to put an exact number on it, but it's hours every day. 

And yeah, it's definitely causing problems. My business schedule is slipping pretty bad. Jobs that I should easily finish in one visit are turning into callbacks and extra checks. It's... it's starting to cost me client confidence, which is tough. And it takes away time I should be spending with the apprentices, teaching them. 

It's affecting my personal life, too. I've been skipping things I used to enjoy doing after work because I'm either still tied up reviewing a job, looking at those photos, or just sitting there worrying about whether I need to drive back out to a site. It just consumes my whole evening sometimes.

symptom_reasoning.S066: The patient confirms engaging in excessive checking behaviors (callbacks, extra checks, reviewing job photos) that consume hours each day and impair work and personal functioning.
